_comment: Group 3 of 3: named checks must pass, on a branch that is up to date.
The check list is EMPTY here and filled in per repo from apply.sh's arguments,
because it is the one thing that legitimately differs: a Node repo requires
'ci / CI', foliot requires 'ci / CI' and 'go / CI', envmesh adds
'scope / pr-scope-guard'. checks.json says which reusable workflow reports which
Only repos that run CI get this group. A required check that never reports does
not fail -- it leaves every PR permanently BLOCKED with every visible check green,
so apply.sh refuses to write this ruleset with no checks.
A caller of a reusable workflow reports '<caller job id> / <inner job name>', so
the name is 'ci / CI', never 'CI'. Derive it from the caller, not from memory.
strict_required_status_checks_policy is true: CI then tests the real merge result,
which is what catches a branch whose tests pass against an API main has changed.
name: required-checks
